caption: The drawing depicts a richly decorated vestment, likely a chasuble, with a white or cream-colored main body. The garment is bordered and segmented by a wide gold or yellow band featuring a pattern of intricate designs. Within the gold-bordered sections are large, colorful floral motifs. These flowers have pink and red petals with green leaves and stems, symmetrically arranged in vertical rows. The central panel contains a prominent red flower surrounded by green foliage, with additional pink flowers and green leaves arranged vertically below. The shoulder and upper chest area also display pink floral motifs. The background inside the gold borders remains a plain white or light cream, emphasizing the vibrancy of the flower and leaf patterns. The overall shape of the vestment is rounded at the bottom and wider at the shoulders, with a simple neckline at the top.
title: Ecclesiastical Vestment
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
